The Belgravians present were Mike Shingles, Fred Paget, 'Glimpy' Jones (Keeping a tight grip on his two main possessions in life, stopwatch and camera) and myself.
Yet win they did and happiest man of the day was undoubtedly Fred Paget who not only gained a team prize but turned the tables on his rival Mike Shingles, in the process.

Married now to Wendy, sister of our own Mike Shingles, he may settle down mentally as well as physically. He has started back on the long grind and, after overcoming and surmounting a few intermediary Everests, he feels convinced that he can still contribute more to his already long service record.
So there is plenty of scope you youngsters for gaining some glory! John Dear(a useful prospect), Mike Shingles and Fred Paget were the only others to show noticeably good form.
10. · J. Davies & M. Shingles · Belgrave H. · 6m. · 372 yds.
T. Hart · 16:28 · M. Shingles · 17:59 · M. Thorpe · 18:26
Of those who were taking part Fairclough, Hart and O'Hara seemed to be favoured to win,and after Mike Shingles had led briefly at the start these three soon drew away from the remainder of the field.

The suprise of the day was sprung by Mike Shingles who all but snatched a place. With the main pack throughout, he finished strongly just ahead of Jack Brown who is always able to shake up his younger opponents.
Jack Brown and Mike Shingles also ran well to finish 7th and 10th respectively,but we still only managed 2nd team behind Maidstone who packed 3,4 and 5.

Bicourt and Hart were always well placed, with Mike Shingles making ground close behind. Dave Cocks and Pete Sadler disappointed and it was left to John Dear to complete our scoring four after a fine run in 59th place.

Mike Shingles and Trevor Hart were both "under the weather" and trailed in 65th and 68th positions. Laurie O'HAra was only 43 seconds outside the county team,in 20th place,and this fast improving runner should soon obtain a red and gold vest.

In fact, with 5 in 49 they looked well set for a sensational 2nd place if their closing runner could finish near at hand, but Mike Shingles is still struggling to regain his old form and could only make 98th,so in a close contest we had to be content with 5th - the same position we made in the "Junior".
Gerry North moved away in the latter stages of the race, doing just enough to win. Mike Shingles ran exceptionally well and was still with O'Hara at the bell.
Mike Shingles and Derek Crookes ran well to finish 13th and 16th respectively. John Dear, who started fast, fell back a little but still finished 19th.

Gerry finished fourth and Laurie O'Hara,Trevor Hart and Mike Shingles all had good runs,Laurie being only 18 secs adrift of Gerry North. Jack Brown also ran well and will no doubt be picking up many Vets prizes come his 40th birthday in August.

How fortunate we were to have the greatly improved Mike Shingles at hand to act as 3rd scorer. He clocked a personal best 9:19 and Belgrave clinched a team win by 6 points from Blackheath and 10 points from T.V.H.

Mike Shingles, who had been below his best for several weeks, was unable to break through the spell and dropped us to 4th on the next stage- a position maintained by Jack Brown on the 3rd leg, and who regained much lost ground in closing up to within 13secs of the runner ahead.

Yet another Belgravian heads south: this time Mike Shingles. Mike, the 'local boy' who this year was beginning to make good, has left us, for a while at least, for the charms (!) of New Zealand !! - and we thought he earnt himself the name of "Night Owl" for his late night training.
Laurie O'Hara (3rd) Trevor Hart (6th) and Mike Shingles (9th) easily took the team prize on this hilly course. Phil King ran very well in leading home the 'B' team which brought up the rear.

Latest news of Mike Shingles now happily married in New Zealand is that he is enjoying the life out there and is now back in full training. He certainly won't be able to get the 'Bels' out of his system as he is now employed as a fireman in Wanganui.

In 1965 Mike Shingles left these shores for the charms of New Zealand! It was interesting to read in 'AW' recently that Beverley Shingles, Mike's kiwi wife, placed 44th out of 308 starters in a marathon at Rotorua.

Several Belgravians can be found amongst the many photographs including Jack Braughton (2nd claim), Charlie Walker, John Bromley, Bill Nankeville, Peter Bagnall, Tom Morrell, Len Herbert, John Davies, Mike Shingles, Charlie Dabbs and Gerry North.
